alt: Component 5 Speaking is worth 60 marks, lasts about 10-12 minutes and is graded 1 to 5 as a separate endorsement. The teacher conducts and marks the test at the centre, then a recorded sample goes to Cambridge for external moderation.
caption: A teacher-run, 60-mark spoken test, moderated by Cambridge and graded 1 to 5.

alt: A timeline of the three parts: Part 1 Presentation (2-3 minutes), Part 2 Discussion of the presentation (3-4 minutes) and Part 3 General Conversation on two or three unseen topics (3-4 minutes, 20 marks).
caption: Presentation, then discussion of it, then an unprepared general conversation.

alt: Paper 1 Reading and Writing and Paper 2 Listening combine into the overall IGCSE grade. Component 5 Speaking is optional and leads to its own separate endorsement graded 1 (high) to 5 (low).
caption: Speaking earns its own 1-5 endorsement; it does not change the IGCSE grade.

alt: A scale from most prepared to most spontaneous. Part 1 uses a topic chosen in advance; Part 2 keeps the topic but the questions are unknown; in Part 3 both topics and questions are unknown, so only broad spoken practice prepares you.
caption: Each part asks for less script and more spontaneous Urdu than the one before.

after: ## Choosing a strong Part 1 presentation topic
alt: Two overlapping circles: a personal interest and Urdu-speaking society or culture; a strong topic sits in the overlap. Examples are a regional cuisine, a family tradition, a festival or a piece of Urdu literature, checked for enough depth to sustain both the presentation and the discussion.
caption: Pick where your own interest meets Urdu-speaking culture, with depth for 5-7 minutes of talk.

after: ## Worked example: preparing for the unpredictable general conversation
alt: Four steps: identify the general topic areas, build a vocabulary and opinion-phrase bank for each, practise answering unannounced questions with a teacher or fluent speaker, and aim for natural rather than recited answers.
caption: Prepare words and opinions, not scripts, then practise being surprised.
